title: Scanning paired encodings
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle $\mathcal O$, $r$ a register, $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $c$ a configuration on input $x$. Suppose the transition identities $hP1,hP2$ hold at states $vP1,vP2$ and neither state is an oracle-call state, as asserted by $cP1,cP2$. For every Boolean word $z$, optional last bit $last$, and natural number $q$ satisfying $q+|z|=|x|+1$, assume that for each $k$, the symbol of $x$ at one-based position $q+k$ equals the $k$th bit of $z$, when defined. If scanning the aligned pairs of $z$, with initial previous bit $last$, returns a word $w$, then the run from state $vP1(last)$ at input-head position $q$ reaches state $vW0$ at position $q+|z|-|w|$, which is a valid input-head position. If the scan returns no word, that run halts with a rejecting output. In both cases, the stated reachability or rejection runs avoid oracle-call states before their endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: No oracle calls at vP1 and vP2
c is a configuration on input x
r is a register and p is an integer
For every k, the symbol of x at one-based position q+k agrees with the kth bit of z when defined
Scan result condition: scanPairs(last,z)=some w, or scanPairs(last,z)=none
